transcript:
Meeting header: Date 2026-03-05 10:00 PST, Duration ~52 minutes. Attendees listed above. Quick notes: recording enabled.

Summary: 52-minute demo/walkthrough of Redwood Console per-route cost analytics. Focus on how to attribute spend to product routes, handle tail latency routes with Dedicated, and savings opportunities via caching and smaller quantized models.

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from Redwood inference i run the west account. can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Maya Chen: yep loud and clear, thanks lena.
[00:10] Lena Park: awesome. quick agenda, we'll go through the Console: route-level dashboards, cost breakouts, route tagging and attribution, then a short bit on Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, and finish with Q and A and next steps. Mateo will jump into the technical bits.
[00:24] Ravi Patel: sounds good. for context we want line of sight on route spend per product feature - search, summarization, chat, embeddings. also want to see impact of caching.
[00:35] Mateo Ruiz: perfect, i'll share my screen, let me know if the screen share looks weird.
[00:42] [screenshare starts] Mateo Ruiz: ok pulling up the Console, this is the tenant overview, here's total utilization by model family and then we have Routes tab, i'll click in.
[01:05] Mateo Ruiz: so routes are how customers map their endpoints, you can tag routes by team, product, and environment - dev/stage/prod - and that drives the per-route breakdown.
[01:18] Sofia Torres: quick question, can we retroactively tag historic traffic? sometimes we onboard routes that are unlabeled.
[01:25] Mateo Ruiz: yes, you can apply tags to existing routes and the historical metrics re-aggregate in the UI, there's an on-demand reprocessing job. note for very large accounts it can take a couple hours.
[01:36] [01:40] Lena Park: that's super useful for teams migrating to Redwood.
[01:43] Mateo Ruiz: moving on, here's the cost waterfall for a selected route - tokens, model execution, GPU time, and then optional add-ons like request-level tracing. you'll see a per-token cost column and a per-minute GPU cost.
[02:05] Ian Good: is the token cost normalized across different model variants, say gpt-like vs llama variants?
[02:11] Mateo Ruiz: good question, the breakdown is based on the actual model variant used. so if you route to a quantized variant, the unit cost shows lower GPU time and lower model execution cost. caveat: the per-token label is more of an abstracted unit we use across the catalog.
[02:27] [02:30] Ravi Patel: how do you attribute cache hits? our concern is that lots of small repeat requests might be masked.
[02:36] Mateo Ruiz: we surface cache hit rate as a column; cache-hit tokens are shown separately and cost attribution removes the execution cost for those tokens. we also show the delta if cache wasn't present - estimated compute saved.
[02:49] Olga Ivanov: security question - where does that cache live? is it in customer VPC for private deployments?
[02:56] Mateo Ruiz: depends on deployment: hosted cache in Redwood-managed infra for hosted API, and for Private we can place cache within the customer VPC/on-prem. explains why some customers choose private for PII workloads.
[03:10] [03:15] Lena Park: i want to highlight the route-level SLA panel on the right, you can set SLOs per route and the Console overlays latency percentiles with cost.
[03:27] Sofia Torres: nice, so if we set a strict p99 we can see the cost impact.
[03:31] Mateo Ruiz: exactly. here's a live example, i bumped p99 target and you can see simulated cost increasing because routing changes to Dedicated variants for tail handling.
[03:46] [03:50] Maya Chen: can the Console simulate different autoscale policies? we want to see burst cost.
[03:56] Mateo Ruiz: yes there's a simulation tool in Optimize - you can toggle burst buffer, reserved capacity, and change instance mixes. it will produce a projected spend and expected latency curve.
[04:10] Lena Park: i'll show the Optimize suggestions briefly, it's doing workload analysis and recommending batching or quantization with an estimated savings column.
[04:20] [04:25] Mateo Ruiz: i want to call out routing policies - you can create a policy that sends low-latency requests to Dedicated with an automatic fallback to hosted variants when Dedicated saturates. this keeps SLAs but controls cost.
[04:38] Ravi Patel: what about multi-region? we have EU data residency constraints for some routes. can routes be pinned to a region?
[04:46] Mateo Ruiz: yes you can pin routes to a region. we also show per-region cost and you can compare the overhead of cross-region egress.
[04:58] [05:05] Lena Park: i'll pull up a customer example - not HaloAI - masked names - but it shows how they aligned billing to product teams using route tags and saved 23% by re-routing heavy batch requests to quantized variants.
[05:20] Maya Chen: that 23% - was that mostly from quantization or batching?
[05:24] Lena Park: mix of both, quantization gave a big per-inference speedup and batching reduced token overhead.
[05:30] [05:35] Mateo Ruiz: on the technical side, the runtime automatically chooses kernels to accelerate quantized weights, and the Console marks which models are quant-ready.
[05:46] Ian Good: do you support GPUs on premises or do you require specific drivers? our infra team uses older v100 clusters.
[05:53] Mateo Ruiz: we support a wide range; for onsite we have an on-prem package and we recommend NGC drivers and patched CUDA; we do a pre-flight to validate kernel compatibility. older V100s can run but throughput differs.
[06:10] [06:15] Olga Ivanov: for compliance, we need KMS integration and audit logs for model access, is that available in Console?
[06:22] Jules Khan: yes, audit logs are surfaced and for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. we'll share the SOC2 pack and example audit log exports after.
[06:33] Maya Chen: perfect. another operational question - how granular are the cost breakdowns? can i get per-endpoint per-day CSV?
[06:40] Mateo Ruiz: yes you can export daily granularity, and there's an API to pull route-level metrics programmatically.
[06:48] [07:05] Sofia Torres: what about model rollouts - if we push a new model variant, will Console show A/B impact on cost and quality?
[07:12] Mateo Ruiz: we have rollout tools with canaries and A/B testing; Console can show side-by-side cost and eval metrics by route. you can also set automatic fallback if quality drops.
[07:25] [07:30] Ravi Patel: okay practical ask - we have two heavy routes: summarization (short prompts, high QPS) and longform chat (long sequences, low QPS). how would you recommend configuring?
[07:40] Lena Park: summarization is a good candidate for aggressive batching and a smaller quantized model; chat may benefit from prefix/KV cache and Dedicated tail-handling for p99.
[07:50] Mateo Ruiz: also consider model sharding and routing by max token length - short sequences go to a smaller model family automatically.
[07:59] [08:05] Maya Chen: can we see that segmentation in the Console?
[08:08] Mateo Ruiz: yes here's an example where we split traffic by max_length on the routing rules page.
[08:16] [08:20] Ian Good: latency numbers — what p50/p95 can we expect on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[08:27] Mateo Ruiz: depends on model, but Dedicated is engineered for lower variance; for mid-sized models p95 can be 30-40% lower on Dedicated. Hosted is more variable but cost-effective for baseline traffic.
[08:41] [08:46] Lena Park: quick aside on billing - the Console shows both committed reserved capacity amortized and on-demand waterfall so you can see true unit economics.
[08:58] Sofia Torres: do you support chargeback to our internal projects?
[09:02] Mateo Ruiz: yes, route tags map to internal chargeback codes and the export includes cost center fields.
[09:09] [09:15] Ravi Patel: security again - can we enforce RBAC on route creation? we don't want product teams spinning up expensive routes.
[09:22] Jules Khan: yes RBAC controls are available and you can require approval flows for rates or model tiers.
[09:31] [09:35] Olga Ivanov: also interested in encryption at rest for cached KVs.
[09:40] Mateo Ruiz: supported in Private deployments, and for hosted we offer encryption with customer-managed keys in some plans. we'll follow up with details.
[09:52] [10:00] Lena Park: i'll now demo the per-route spend drilldown - this is a synthetic route from a demo account: you get a timeline, top contributing models, cache hit rate overlay, and cost per 1k requests.
[10:20] Maya Chen: can we set alerts when route spend crosses a budget?
[10:24] Mateo Ruiz: yes alerts and automated throttling policies exist. you can also set 'soft caps' that notify product owners.
[10:33] [10:40] Sofia Torres: about the Optimize recommendations - how do you validate they won't harm quality?
[10:46] Lena Park: we recommend running suggestions in a canary first and Console evaluation hooks can run prompt sets to compare quality metrics. Optimize will flag regressions before rollout.
[10:59] [11:05] Ravi Patel: for the pilot we want 2 routes instrumented for 2 weeks to validate cost projections and latency. is that feasible?
[11:12] Lena Park: absolutely, we often do a short pilot. typically we instrument routes, run sampling, and run Optimize suggestions in a non-blocking canary.
[11:22] [11:26] Maya Chen: what would the pilot cost look like?
[11:29] Lena Park: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet. for pilots we sometimes provide credits depending on commitment.
[11:36] [11:40] Ian Good: any customer's run into surprise egress charges when routing cross-region?
[11:44] Mateo Ruiz: yes if you don't pin routes. Console shows cross-region egress in the cost waterfall and Optimize can recommend replication if egress outweighs benefits.
[11:55] [12:00] Olga Ivanov: procedural question - we have procurement windows and need SSO/SAML bridge details for IdP.
[12:07] Jules Khan: we support SAML2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. we'll attach a tech brief to the follow-up.
[12:15] [12:20] Lena Park: closing loop, any more product questions?
[12:23] Maya Chen: one more — how do you recommend we present console metrics to execs? like a simple dashboard?
[12:29] Lena Park: we can create a custom executive dashboard with high-level KPIs: daily spend, top 3 routes by cost, p99 latency, and projected monthly.
[12:39] [12:45] Sofia Torres: that would be great for our finance review.
[12:48] [12:55] Mateo Ruiz: quick demo note — there may be slight transcript pauses and the UI shows live re-aggregation.
[13:02] [13:10] Lena Park: ok let's do a short recap and next steps. Recap: showed Console route-level cost, caching attribution, Optimize savings, and rollout/fallback patterns. HaloAI's primary asks: per-route cost projection, SOC2/KMS details, and a technical deep dive on private deployment.
[13:28] Lena Park: next steps again — lena to send pricing sheet and per-route projection, avery to send security docs and KMS notes, schedule technical deep dive with ravi and mateo.
[13:44] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, look forward to the docs and the deep dive.
[13:48] Ravi Patel: thanks, excited to run the pilot.
[13:50] Lena Park: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD with notes and links.

End of transcript.

References / shared artifacts: console screenshots (sent post-call), per-route cost template (will be shared), SOC2 pack link placeholder.
